home.kicker: A NEW WAY TO SEE THE COSMOS
home.heroDescription: Explore the universe in 102 shades of infrared with NASA’s SPHEREx all-sky survey.
home.introDescription: SPHEREx is mapping the entire sky in near-infrared light—collecting spectra that help scientists investigate cosmic history, galaxies, and the ingredients of planet-forming systems. These tools connect to the NASA/IPAC IRSA public archive.
home.explorerDescription: Search public SPHEREx DR1 products at any celestial coordinate.
home.timeDescription: Review available observations—and compare only verified matching image data.
home.spectrumDescription: Understand the mission’s spectral range and inspect available archive metadata.
home.detectorDescription: Learn what reliable time-domain analysis needs before calling a change.
home.imageNotice: Reference imagery is from NASA’s public image library, not SPHEREx survey products. Archive observations are identified separately and linked to their IRSA records.

detector.title: Change Detector
detector.description: A responsible transient search starts with matched, calibrated observations—not side-by-side pictures alone.
detector.noCandidatesHelp: This tool does not process SPHEREx FITS pixel arrays. No brightness, centroid, or detection significance is inferred from archive metadata.
detector.awaitingHelp: A possible change can only be evaluated after two calibrated SPHEREx images cover the same region and have been spatially aligned. Data quality and instrumental effects must also be assessed.
detector.footprintHelp: Confirm both images cover the same celestial coordinates.
detector.calibrationHelp: Check compatible data releases, units, and processing.
detector.registrationHelp: Align pixels using validated WCS and astrometric references.
detector.artifactsHelp: Inspect masks, PSF differences, coverage, and detector artifacts.
detector.humanHelp: Review candidate sources before interpreting any change.
detector.possibleChangeHelp: An apparent variation warrants further investigation; not a discovery.
detector.candidateHelp: A candidate requires assessment against images and quality flags.
detector.qualityIssueHelp: Artifacts, masks, or mismatched processing limit interpretation.
detector.noChangeHelp: Only appropriate after a valid, sensitivity-aware comparison.

reports.title: Evidence Reports
reports.description: Create a source-linked report of real archive metadata. Measured values are never inferred from file names or reference images.
reports.chooseHelp: Retrieve the SPHEREx DR1 records and build a report that distinguishes archive metadata from measured results.
reports.productsHelp: The report includes a decoded image view from the first selected FITS product. Open another listed product to inspect it. No difference image or measured change is claimed.
reports.noRecords: No public DR1 records returned for this position.
reports.measuredHelp: No flux values, source positions, change scores, or confidence values have been measured. These require image and spectral product processing.
reports.interpretationHelp: There is not enough processed evidence to infer a change or transient. Archive coverage alone is not evidence that an object changed.
reports.source: Source: NASA/IPAC IRSA SIA · SPHEREx DR1 · DOI
reports.emptyHelp: Run an archive query to generate a linked evidence summary for a sky region.

learn.title: Learn SPHEREx
learn.description: A whole-sky map, one spectrum at a time. Here are the ideas behind the mission.
learn.fullName: SPECTRO-PHOTOMETER FOR THE HISTORY OF THE UNIVERSE, EPOCH OF REIONIZATION AND ICES EXPLORER
learn.bannerTitle: SPHEREx gives the sky a spectrum.
learn.bannerText: Instead of observing just a few colors, this NASA space telescope surveys the whole sky in near-infrared light, recording information across many spectral channels.
learn.a1: A NASA space mission that surveys the entire sky in near-infrared light. Its measurements help researchers study cosmic inflation, galaxy history, and the ingredients of star and planet formation.
learn.a2: Infrared is light with wavelengths longer than visible light. It can reveal cool objects and pass through some cosmic dust that obscures visible-light views.
learn.a3: The instrument's linear variable filter records spectral information across a broad 0.75–5.0 μm range. The 102 nominal channels are part of the survey's instrument and data-product design.
learn.a4: Spectroscopy measures how light varies with wavelength. The shape and features of a measured spectrum can help astronomers infer an object's properties—when calibrated data are available.
learn.a5: Repeated observations can help researchers investigate variation, but only after matching sky coverage, calibration, spatial alignment, and image quality.
learn.a6: Scientists check calibrated pixels, source positions, noise, artifacts, and consistency across observations. An apparent difference is a candidate for review—not a discovery.
learn.imagesNotice: These educational images come from NASA’s public image library; they are not labeled as SPHEREx data.

about.title: A lens, not a telescope.
about.description: COSMIC LENS is an independent interface to public SPHEREx archive resources. It is not affiliated with NASA, JPL, Caltech, or the SPHEREx mission team.
about.built1: The app searches NASA/IPAC IRSA’s Simple Image Access v2 service for SPHEREx DR1 records and links directly to the returned data products. Search results and dates are not hard-coded or presented as a total archive count.
about.built2: Image references are fetched from NASA’s public Images API and labeled as reference material. NASA reference imagery is never presented as a SPHEREx observation.
about.limits1: The viewer reads supported 2D FITS images and converts them to PNG. Matched images are registered and sources are detected exploratorily, without calibration or catalogue identification.
about.limits2: Source classifications are unconfirmed. An unmatched detection is not evidence that an object formed or disappeared.

about.dataExplorerSub: Official archive interface for search and visualization
about.siaSub: Standard metadata query endpoint and query parameters

about.ackText: This publication makes use of data products from the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx), which is a joint project of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory and the California Institute of Technology, and is funded by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

explanation.common: This unclassified source was detected in both observations. No significant change was flagged by the exploratory measurements.
explanation.new_candidate: This source was detected only in the later image. Sensitivity, noise, image quality, and observation differences can explain an unmatched detection; this is not evidence of a newly formed object.
explanation.not_detected_later: This source was detected earlier but not reliably detected later. Sensitivity, noise, image quality, and observation differences can explain the non-detection.
explanation.brightness_candidate: This source was detected in both images and its measured flux difference passed exploratory thresholds. Calibration, PSF, and data-quality effects still require review.
explanation.position_candidate: The measured source positions differ after image registration. Astrometric and measurement uncertainties require further review.
